trajectory.thought: The leader is a seeded baseline (mean over pool3, 9 stable models) and the verdict is "indistinguishable" — the runner-up differs by only 0.004. With unstable ranking (Kendall τ ≈ −0.07), high error correlation (mean 0.81), and only 3 validation windows, there is no statistical basis to prefer any alternative. The robust mean over the most consistent subset is well-matched to this strongly trending, strongly seasonal series where most models capture the same underlying signal.

action_args.justification: Strong trend (0.999) and seasonality (1.0) mean most models capture the same structured signal; high error correlation (0.812) and unstable cross-window ranking (τ≈−0.07) argue against fitted weights or small subsets. A robust mean over the 9 most consistently-ranked models avoids overfitting to 3 noisy validation windows while retaining the benefit of averaging out idiosyncratic noise. The leader is a seed and the margin to the runner-up is statistically indistinguishable, so further testing is unlikely to yield a real gain.
